question: Assume today is 2026-09-12. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of passengers at London Heathrow Airport in September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics.

target.what: Total passengers counted at London Heathrow Airport in Heathrow's published monthly traffic statistics for the calendar month of September 2026
target.publisher: Heathrow Airport Limited / Heathrow Airport Holdings (Heathrow monthly traffic statistics)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: Heathrow's headline monthly passenger total for London Heathrow only, covering the full calendar month and counting passengers according to the publisher's definition, including its treatment of transfer/transit passengers. Material alternative: terminal or origin-and-destina

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers should be anchored by previous September levels, adjusted by 2026 year-to-date growth and the normal September-to-August seasonal ratio; published adjacent 2026 months constrain the current level.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly total passengers for September 2024 and September 2025; published 2026 January-August monthly totals, especially July and August 2026; 2025 August and September values to compute year-on-year growth and the September/August ratio; notes on definition and revisions.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly traffic statistics September 2025 passengers

candidates.perspective: UK Civil Aviation Authority airport statistics compiler
candidates.hypothesis: CAA monthly airport data for Heathrow provides an independent passenger series that can validate or fill gaps in Heathrow's own history after aligning terminal/transit definitions and reporting periods.
candidates.data_to_find: CAA Heathrow monthly terminal passengers for September 2025 and latest 2026 months available before cutoff; definitions distinguishing terminal, transit, and total passengers; if CAA monthly is unavailable, use UK airport statistics or ONS transport data at the closest available scope.
search_hints: CAA airport data Heathrow monthly passengers 2026
UK airport statistics Heathrow September 2025 passengers

candidates.perspective: airline schedule and seat-capacity data provider such as OAG, Cirium, or ACL
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers are approximately total scheduled seats on all Heathrow arrivals and departures in the month multiplied by achieved load factor, adjusted for cancellations and the airport's passenger definition; schedules for September are largely known before the cutoff.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow September 2026 scheduled seat capacity on both arrivals and departures, or total scheduled seats by month; comparable achieved load factors for Heathrow or closely comparable UK/European airports in September 2025 and 2026 year-to-date; scheduled cancellation rates.

candidates.perspective: air traffic and airport operations analyst
candidates.hypothesis: Monthly passengers are approximately air transport movements multiplied by average passengers per ATM; Heathrow movement counts, ACL/NATS schedules, and historical passengers per movement provide a flow-based cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly air transport movements for September 2025 and latest 2026 months; average passengers per ATM implied by Heathrow monthly statistics; September 2026 scheduled or allocated ATMs from Heathrow, ACL, or NATS; if movement schedules are unavailable, annual movement cap and September share.

candidates.hypothesis: September is a transition month after the summer peak; historical September/August and September/July passenger ratios plus calendar effects such as school return, business travel resumption, and bank holidays can transfer the 2026 August level into September.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passenger totals over 2015-2025 to estimate stable September seasonal ratios; September 2026 calendar, school holiday dates, major London events, and any known demand-shifting holidays; day-of-week composition if available.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly passenger seasonality September August

candidates.perspective: Heathrow, airline, and aviation industry outlook
candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow or industry annual 2026 passenger guidance, allocated with historical monthly shares, gives an independent level check; airline capacity guidance for London/UK in Q3 2026 may constrain September activity.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow 2026 annual passenger forecast or guidance published before 2026-09-12; IATA or ACI Europe UK/Europe 2026 passenger forecasts; IAG/British Airways or major Heathrow airlines' Q3 2026 capacity and load-factor guidance; monthly allocation shares from Heathrow history.

candidates.perspective: airport operational risk and news monitor
candidates.hypothesis: Known disruptions, strikes, weather, security incidents, ATC constraints, runway works, or policy changes affecting September 2026 could shift achieved passengers away from the schedule/history relationship; measurable cancelled movements or seats should adjust the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow operational notices and capacity restrictions for September 2026; UK/European strike calendars; ATC disruption notices; severe weather events; airline cancellations or schedule reductions announced before cutoff; travel policy changes effective in September 2026.

methods.rationale: Estimates September 2026 as the same share of Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative passengers as September 2025 was of Jan-Aug 2025. Uses only Heathrow monthly cumulative data; p3 minus p1 reconstructs Jan-Aug 2025 and matches p149. Failure mode: if the 2026 monthly profile shifts materially, especially from the early-September disruption or a different summer peak, the cumulative share changes.

methods.label: m3

p58.role: September 2025-August 2026 Heathrow trailing 12-month total passengers, current annual run-rate proxy

p82.role: 2025 calendar-year Heathrow total passengers, denominator for September's historical share of annual traffic

methods.rationale: Uses the current trailing-12-month level as an annual run-rate and applies September 2025's share of the 2025 calendar year. p82 is rounded but corroborated by CAA p135 84.463M. Failure mode: the trailing 12 months include the weak 2026 months and may not represent the September run-rate if seasonality or the disruption shifts passengers between months.

methods.label: m4

p128.role: January-August 2026 Heathrow total passengers year-on-year percentage change

methods.rationale: Simple year-on-year route: September 2026 equals September 2025 times the Jan-Aug 2026 YTD change. p128 is -0.4%, reflecting recent weakness. Failure mode: September 2026 YoY may differ from YTD, especially because August 2026 was -2.1% (p127) and the early-September disruption is not fully captured.
methods.error: input p128 must be positive for lognormal sampling

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m5
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p159: The p1/p159 ratio uses September 2025 passengers over August 2025 movements; the denominator evidence is a different period from the September numerator, so it does not denote the matching Septe

kept.name: September 2026 Heathrow passenger loss from early-September NATS disruption
kept.rationale: Based on p162/p163: 1,477 UK flights cancelled over 8-9 September 2026. Heathrow is roughly one-fifth of UK movements (p59 monthly ATMs versus p43 daily UK movements), and at about 183 passengers/ATM (p141) a full loss would be roughly 0.7% of a 7M+ month. Rebooking and passenger reaccommodation red
kept.applies_when: The NATS disruption actually affected Heathrow movements and the net passenger loss was not fully offset by rebooking within September.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Heathrow had no material cancellations, or that disrupted passengers were fully reaccommodated within September.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
